<header>Sūtrasthāna-Ch. 19. (143)</header>

The expert physician should repeatedly extract the impurities from the wounds of <term>kapha</term> <gloss>phlegm humor</gloss> and <term>vāyu</term> <gloss>wind/air humor</gloss> in various ways. 39. Pressing the wound from below, he should allow it to drain according to the direction of the pores, and he should properly join all the hidden closures and joints. 40. In joining the lips, he should proceed as previously described; and the physician who understands joints should apply the appropriate bandages for setting bones, after reflecting upon it with his own intelligence. 41.

Uttiṣṭhano nipaṇṇasya śayanaṃ cāpi gacchataḥ ||
Gacchato vividhādyairnaiḥ nasya duṣyati sai vraṇaḥ || 42 ||
Sandhyasthikoṣṭhaprāptāśca śirā-snāyugatāstathau ||
Tathaivagāḍhagaṃbhīrāḥ sarvato viṣamasthitāḥ ||
Naite sādhayituṃ śakyā ṛte vandhairbhavanti hi || 43 ||

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the Sūtrasthāna in the Suśruta Saṃhitā. 18.

For a person who is rising, sitting, going to bed, walking, or riding, the wound does not suffer <note>i.e., become aggravated or painful</note> (once the proper bandage is applied). 42. Wounds located in the joints, bones, or viscera; wounds involving the veins and tendons; and wounds that are dense, deep, or uneven on all sides cannot be treated without the proper bandages. 43.

Thus ends the Hindi translation of the eighteenth chapter of the Sūtrasthāna of the Suśruta Saṃhitā, by Pandit Muralidhar Sharma. 18.

### The Nineteenth Chapter 19.

Now we shall explain the chapter on the care of the wounded <term>Vraṇitopāsanīya</term>.

Here we commence the explanation of the chapter on the conduct regarding wounds.

The physician should first look for a dwelling for the wounded person, and that dwelling should be constructed in a place with a favorable environment. 1. In a house with a favorable environment, which is clean and free from wind and sunlight, and sheltered from drafts, there will be no physical, accidental, or mental diseases. 2. He should prepare a spacious, well-spread, and pleasant bed with the head toward the east, provided with weapons <note>traditionally for protection against malevolent spirits</note>. 3. The wounded person will have ease of movement on a well-spread bed. The gods dwell in the eastern direction, therefore one should not have the head oriented toward that direction. 4.

(Verse 42) Bond-related.

<summary>This page concludes the eighteenth chapter on wound management and begins the nineteenth chapter concerning the appropriate living environment and care for a patient with wounds.</summary>
